title: The Wrong Number
subtitle: Understanding changes the moral shape of a conflict
sourceCredit: Lori Tucker-Sullivan · The Moth Radio Hour, “Beef”

shot.title: Two burdens, one ring
shot.direction: An oversized telephone dominates a room beside an ill partner; keep the hospital details restrained.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: A quiet care room with the woman seated near her resting husband's plain bed, one hand on the arm of her real chair. An ordinary desk telephone on a small bedside table casts an oversized ink shadow across the wall, making the interruption feel huge without making the handset physically impossible to lift. Her face is tired and alert to the ring. Keep the husband restful and secondary, with no named diagnosis, dramatic monitor or invented medical intervention.

shot.title: The receiver shakes
shot.direction: The receiver gives one insistent shake, not an endless alarm.

beats.caption: Where is he? Why won’t anyone tell me?
beats.speaker: CALLER

shot.title: The accusation arrives
shot.direction: A sharp caller’s bubble intrudes; the woman’s grip tightens.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: The woman holds the actual receiver naturally to her ear, fingers wrapped around its handle and elbow supported near her torso. Her free hand braces against the chair arm as her jaw tightens; the resting husband remains behind her, separate from the phone interaction. A sharp dark speech-shape near the receiver suggests the caller's accusation with no words. Her own posture answers sharply. The oversized phone shadow remains an emotional metaphor, not a giant prop attached to a tiny hand.

beats.caption: You have no right to call us like this.
beats.speaker: WOMAN

shot.title: Anger answers

shot.title: A breath between rooms
shot.direction: The line goes quiet long enough to hear a change in the caller.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: A single wide illustration clearly separates two ordinary rooms with a soft vertical wall division. Left, the woman has paused mid-reply beside her husband's bed, receiver still at her ear. Right, the caller sits alone at a modest table in a different room, one hand holding his own telephone and the other searching an empty patch of tabletop. His posture is anxious and uncertain. No shared furniture, connecting doorway or visual suggestion they occupy the same building.

shot.title: The other room opens
shot.direction: A second panel reveals the caller as a separate person in a difficult room.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

beats.caption: I’m frightened. I don’t know who else to ask.
beats.speaker: CALLER

shot.title: Fear behind the words
shot.direction: The caller’s expression and searching hand replace the earlier threatening scale.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: Inside the caller's separate room, show his whole seated body at the table, shoulders drawn inward, brows raised with fear, eyes searching beyond the phone rather than glaring. His free hand opens helplessly beside an ordinary unmarked scrap of paper while his other hand holds the receiver securely. Chair, hips and feet align naturally. Keep the room modest and vague; do not invent a missing person's identity, financial cause, hospital or new evidence.

shot.title: Listening without interrupting
shot.direction: Her shoulders lower; she stops forming a reply and listens.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: Back in the woman's care room, her shoulders have lowered and the braced free hand now rests loosely on her thigh. She listens into an ordinary-sized receiver, mouth closed before a softer reply, eyes showing recognition rather than triumph. The husband remains resting in the same bed, reminding us that her burden continues. The exaggerated shadow has thinned into an ordinary telephone shadow. Keep her face and actual connected fingers readable; no sudden smile that erases the day.

beats.caption: I didn’t understand who was on the other end.
beats.speaker: WOMAN

shot.title: Who was on the other end
shot.direction: The telephone returns gradually to ordinary scale; both rooms remain distinct.

shot.title: Both having a terrible day
shot.direction: She offers understanding without pretending the difficulties have disappeared.
shot.soundDirection: Ring, brittle receiver noise, distant breathing, then soft room tone.

illustration.direction: Return to the two separate rooms in quiet balanced proportions, divided clearly and softly, not joined. The woman sits near her resting husband with a relaxed telephone grip; the caller sits alone at his own table, shoulders a little less defensive. Both receivers are ordinary, both faces tired but less hardened. Keep the distinct sage and mauve clothing and each room's unchanged furniture. No reunion, cure, discovered person or solved practical problem; the shared thing is understanding across distance.
